current_answer: As of 20 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. The fresh change is that the surrounding system is visibly moving: OpenAI’s status history records recent GPT-5.6 paid-plan and API errors, managed-agent delays, and an Agent API container-overbilling incident; Google’s Antigravity 09-2026 release changes local tool and file-operation contracts. A provider-authored Anthropic retrospective reports rising internal coding-session success, while public drift monitors disagree or measure different tasks. Users are switching because quota, capacity, access, and task fit change before a model-quality test can run. Record the requested and served model, route, tool contract, task budget, warning/stop state, outcome, and allowance before calling degradation.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad model decline is proven. The surrounding system changed: incidents, tool contracts, drift estimands, quota, and task fit now need one receipt.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven; calm current status pages narrow declared outages but do not measure task quality.
OpenAI’s recent history records resolved paid-plan GPT-5.6 and API errors, managed-agent delays, and an Agent API container-overbilling incident.
Google’s Antigravity 09-2026 release changes local tool and file-operation contracts; migration failure can look like model degradation without a weight change.

Anthropic reports rising internal Claude Code session success, while AI Drift Detector flags broad movement on a fixed coding board and Pondral reports stable AI-search visibility; these are different estimands.
Current Codex users describe quota pressure, capacity or task-fit variability, and switching; self-selected threads are valuable intake, not prevalence or capability evidence.
NextReset and Codex Pulse reinforce a symptom-first fixed-task receipt; the public edge is causal explanation and a reversible action, not another generic score.
Reader move: record task, requested and served model, route, tool-contract version, budget, warning/stop state, outcome, allowance, and switching reason before switching or calling degradation.
uncertainty: No matched longitudinal cross-provider task series, provider-served-model receipt, provider ledger, representative denominator, human pilot, or willingness-to-pay evidence is available.
Official status histories and release notes establish declared events and contracts, not the prevalence or task-quality effect for a reader’s account.
AI Drift Detector, Pondral, and Anthropic’s internal series use different tasks, operators, samples, and estimands; their disagreement is informative but not a common verdict.
Community switching reports are self-selected and may reflect quota, routing, capacity, plan, context, or task-fit changes rather than core capability.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source research completed 20 September 2026. The broad call remains no capability decline proven, while provider incidents, tool-contract migration, public-monitor disagreement, and quota-driven switching are now explicit evidence lanes.
